name: kestrel-vale
about: A scripted interviewee for an omnichannel outdoor retailer: three lines of business, twelve roles over four levels, three processes over seven systems, nine document types with review chains, four months with an incident, a departure and a mid-history policy change, and twelve eval intents, three per level. Every question's first answer is refused on purpose, so the refusal loop runs on every layer.

episodes.name: SupplierTermsCycle
episodes.detail: One month of the commercial desk: the pipeline reviewed, one agreement legally reviewed and signed, funding recognised against signed plans. The legal gate is the episode's spine; signature is caused by clearance, never beside it.

fact_kinds.text: Meridian Foods Group, under the FY26 joint business plan

invariants.detail: The annual plan's counterparty belongs to no month; the monthly cycle recognises against it.
The committed annual value is agreed at signature and holds for the term.
The rate is a term of the agreement, not a monthly negotiation.

fact_kinds.text: Cleared for signature; indemnity clause amended at review
Volume-commitment exposure if category resets mid-term; mitigated by the quarterly true-up clause

events.summary: The commercial desk reviewed the trade pipeline: value under negotiation and the agreements carrying it, ahead of this month's signature.
Legal and controls review of the lead agreement closed: cleared for signature with the indemnity clause amended.
The joint business plan was signed following clearance: committed annual value and rebate rate now on the record.
Monthly trade funding was recognised against signed agreements, at the contracted rebate rate.

artifacts.rationale: The desk's monthly account of what is in negotiation and what signed; the document a 'what deals are in flight' question retrieves.
The contract of record: parties, term, committed value, rate; and the clearance it relied on, by reference.
The review the signature cites: scope, findings, and the one risk worth carrying forward on the record.
The paper the board reads on trading terms: what signed, at what rate, and what it earned this month.

carry_forward.detail: The annual plan's counterparty does not change monthly; month N recognises against month 1's signature.
The committed annual value is a term of the signed plan.
So is the rate; a rate that renegotiated itself monthly would contradict LORE-TRADE-FUNDING.

role_slots.purpose: review the pipeline and sign the agreement once cleared
run the legal and controls review; may hold the agreement
book the monthly funding against signed plans; never the negotiator

evaluation.detail: The gate is the story: signature follows clearance. The questions worth authoring are the ones whose confident wrong answer is the bigger, better-known number one document over.

families.question: What rebate rate is the group contractually entitled to under the signed joint business plan, as at {period}?
families.answer: {value}; the rate the trade agreement states. The pipeline review quotes it secondhand; the agreement is the record.
families.reasoning: Two documents carry the rate and only one is the contract.

abstentions.question: What hourly rate does the group pay its external counsel for trade agreement reviews?
abstentions.reasoning: Reviews are performed in-house by the legal and controls function; no external counsel, and no rate, exists anywhere in the corpus.

episodes.name: ProgrammeSteering
episodes.detail: Monthly steering of the checkout and loyalty replatform: status reported, spend booked cumulatively against a fixed envelope, risks counted and carried. The programme LORE-REPLATFORM promises is the one this episode papers.

fact_kinds.text: Amber; conversion volatility holding the cutover gate

invariants.detail: The envelope is fixed by the funding decision; a programme that rebases its own budget is the defect LORE-REPLATFORM names.

events.summary: The programme reported its monthly status: state, spend against the envelope, and the next milestone.
The steering committee met on the reported position and recorded its decisions and the risks it chose to carry.

artifacts.rationale: The monthly report the funded programme owes its governance; status, burn, and what is left of a fixed envelope.
Decisions with the figures they were taken on, and the risks the committee accepted; the record a 'who decided' question retrieves.
The delivery manager's weekly status: where the build stands, what it cost this period, what is due next.

carry_forward.detail: This month opens where last month closed; cumulative spend is the one figure here whose whole meaning is its history, and the first month opens at zero because nothing had been spent, not because nothing was recorded.

role_slots.purpose: report status and spend; owns the plan
chair steering and own the decisions

evaluation.detail: Cumulative spend against a fixed envelope is the question shape here; the confident wrong answer is always this month's burn.

families.question: How much of the replatform programme's fixed envelope had been spent by the end of {period}?
families.answer: {value} of the envelope; cumulative to date, not the month's burn.
families.reasoning: The status report states both figures; the trap is answering with the period spend.

abstentions.question: Which external systems integrator is delivering the checkout replatform?
abstentions.reasoning: The programme is delivered by the platform engineering team; no integrator is engaged or named anywhere in the corpus.

episodes.name: IncidentReview
episodes.detail: One month of service operations: incidents triaged as they land, then reviewed, with the month's service health on the record. Review follows triage, never beside it.

fact_kinds.text: Reviewed: the checkout timeout traced to a certificate rotation, with the runbook amended

events.summary: Service operations triaged the month's incidents: how many stayed open and how long restoration took.
The post-incident review was published: what caused the month's worst incident and what changed.

artifacts.rationale: The incident manager's status: what is open and how quickly service came back.
The director's review of service health and the lesson the month's review recorded.

role_slots.purpose: triage incidents and report what stays open
run the post-incident review and publish it

sections.heading: Pipeline position
sections.purpose: The value under negotiation and how many agreements carry it. State the number that moved since last month first; a pipeline review that opens with the total is a review of nothing.

sections.heading: This month's signature
sections.purpose: The agreement that signed: who with, its annual value, and the rebate rate agreed. One deal argued properly, not a list.

sections.heading: Funding recognised
sections.purpose: What this month's ledger books against signed agreements. Recognition follows the signed plan, and this figure is the month's answer to 'did it'.

sections.heading: Parties and term
sections.purpose: Who the agreement binds, stated as the contract states it. Formal register; this is the document the others quote.

sections.heading: Commercial terms
sections.purpose: The annual committed value and the rebate rate. Numbers with their basis, no commentary; a contract that argues is a memo.

sections.heading: Review and clearance
sections.purpose: The legal review outcome this signature relied on, by reference. A signed agreement citing no clearance is the defect the review gate exists to prevent.

sections.heading: Scope of review
sections.purpose: What was reviewed: the agreement, its counterparty, the value at stake. Written so a later reader can tell whether this note covers the document in their other hand.

sections.heading: Findings and clearance
sections.purpose: The outcome and the one risk worth recording. 'Cleared' and 'held' are the vocabulary; if held, say what unheld it or would.

sections.heading: Status
sections.purpose: The programme's state in one word its own governance defines, and the next milestone with its date. The reader is deciding whether to escalate, not learning the project exists.

sections.heading: Spend against envelope
sections.purpose: Cumulative spend against the fixed envelope, and this month's burn. The envelope does not move; say plainly how much of it is left.

sections.heading: Decisions
sections.purpose: What the steering committee decided, with the figures it decided on. Minutes record decisions and who owns them; discussion belongs in the memory of the people who had it.

sections.heading: Risks accepted
sections.purpose: The open risks the committee saw and chose to carry. A count with the top one named, not a register.

sections.heading: Terms signed
sections.purpose: What the group committed to and at what rate; one agreement, argued properly.

sections.heading: Funding earned
sections.purpose: What the month's ledger recognised against signed terms, and whether it tracks the plan.

sections.heading: Assurance
sections.purpose: The review the signature relied on, by outcome.

sections.heading: Where the build stands
sections.purpose: State and the next milestone, first.

sections.heading: This period's cost
sections.purpose: The period's burn, never the cumulative figure.

sections.heading: Open incidents
sections.purpose: How many incidents are still open and which matter.

sections.heading: Restoration
sections.purpose: How long restoration took on average, and the outlier.
